market.what: chemicals and media sold to remove phosphate (WWTP iron/alum coagulants, P sorbents, lake binders), world
market.method: avg of 2 reports: P-removing agents $890M (2024) and chemical-precipitation P removal $850M (2024); cross-check ferric chloride $978M x 60% water use = ~$590M. Selective sorbents are a small slice (Phoslock 2024 sales A$0.76M)

value.logic: Polishing to <=0.1 mg/L with alum costs $160-430/kg P. Est. 15 km3/yr effluent at tight limits x 0.4 g P/m3 = 6 kt P/yr; selective sorbent at ~$60/kg P saves ~$150/kg -> ~$0.9B/yr (est.). Ag drain filters today cost $100-1,300/kg P: extra upside not counted
value.revenue_logic: Polishing media spend if adopted ~6 kt P x $60/kg = $360M; K14 binder in a partner resin at ~5% share -> ~$18M, plus ag filter media ~$2M (est.)
value.margin_logic: specialty grafted resin/media sold per m3; binder cost small vs resin price

trend.drivers: EU UWWTD recast 2024/3019 (P 0.5-0.7 mg/L, tertiary at >=150k PE); US permits down to 0.05 mg/L; Lake Erie / H2Ohio runoff programs
trend.deadline: 2039: EU UWWTD tertiary (P) treatment at all plants >=150k PE

direct_startups: CAPTure system (Kieser & Associates, ag drainage P filter)
competition.notes: Iron/alum precipitation dominates and is cheap at 0.5-1 mg/L; the gap is ultra-low polishing and runoff. Hybrid iron-oxide resins (HAIX, FerrIX) are the bar. Phoslock sales collapsed to A$0.76M in 2024; H2Ohio cut from $270M to ~$165M

lab.synth: 1-2 step custom: cyclic amidinium (aldehyde + diamine condensation), 3 variants; then grafting onto a resin bead adds ~6 wk
lab.test: binding vs Cl-/SO4 by NMR/ITC titration, then batch isotherms + small column in real effluent; orthophosphate by EPA 365.1 (university water lab)
lab.logic: synth 6 wk + grafting 6 wk + tests 4 wk; 3 x $6k synth + $15k grafting + ~300 EPA 365.1 samples at $7-22 (~$5k) + $7k ITC/column work

sale.gates: resin-partner scale-up ~1 yr; WWTP or tile-drain pilot 1 season; fits NRCS 782 P removal practice for farm cost-share
